questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of opportunity cost?
options: The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
The total amount of money spent on a decision
The value of all the alternatives added together
The cost of a missed sales opportunity
questions.why: It is the benefit forgone from the single next best alternative. Not the cash spent, and not the sum of everything you did not choose.
whyNot: That is the financial cost. The opportunity cost is what that money could otherwise have achieved.
Only the next best alternative counts, not all of them.
A common misreading. Opportunity cost applies to every choice, not just lost sales.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: accepting less of one objective in order to achieve more of another?
options: Trade-off
Opportunity cost
Scarcity
Satisficing
questions.why: A trade-off is the exchange itself: less margin for more share, more quality for more cost. It is the normal condition of business decisions, not a mistake.
whyNot: Opportunity cost is the value of what is given up, which is closely related but not the same as the exchange.
Scarcity is why choices have to be made at all.
Satisficing is accepting a satisfactory rather than maximum outcome.

questions.stem: A business has $40,000 and three options returning $12,000, $9,000 and $3,400 a year. It chooses the $12,000 option. What is the opportunity cost?
options: $9,000 a year
$12,400 a year
$3,400 a year
questions.why: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone, which is the $9,000 option. Not the money spent, and not the two rejected options added together.
whyNot: That is the financial cost of the investment.
This adds the two rejected returns together. Only the best of them counts.
That is the worst option, not the next best.

questions.stem: Why does opportunity cost apply to a founder's time as well as their money?
options: Time and attention are finite resources, so using them on one thing means not using them elsewhere
Time has no financial value
Only money is a scarce resource
Founders have unlimited time
questions.why: A founder who spends three months opening a second site has given up whatever those three months could have achieved at the first one. For a small business the founder's attention is often the scarcest resource of all.
whyNot: It has a very real value, measured by what else could have been done with it.
Staff, premises, management attention and time are all scarce.
The opposite is closer to the truth in a small business.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of scarcity?
options: Resources are limited relative to the wants they could satisfy, so choices must be made
A business has run out of cash
A product is temporarily out of stock
There are few competitors in a market
questions.why: Scarcity is the underlying condition that makes opportunity cost exist. If resources were unlimited, nothing would have to be given up.
whyNot: That is a liquidity problem, a specific consequence rather than the concept.
That is a stock-out, an operational issue.
That describes market structure.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly describes a common business trade-off?
options: Higher quality against higher cost
Higher quality against higher quality
Lower price against lower costs
More staff against more staff
questions.why: Better materials, better training and better service all cost more. That is the design mix and the cost efficiency tension in one, and it recurs throughout the unit.
whyNot: Not a trade-off; both sides are the same thing.
A lower price does not produce lower costs. These do not trade off against each other.
Again not a trade-off.

questions.stem: Why might a business choose an option with a lower financial return?
options: It may carry less risk, or diversify income, or fit the owner's objectives better
Lower returns are always preferable
Financial returns cannot be compared
Businesses never consider risk
questions.why: Return is only one criterion. An option that returns less but reduces dependence on a single income stream, or cuts debt, can be the better decision. Saying this is exactly what lifts a recommendation into evaluation.
whyNot: No, and the point is that return is not the only criterion.
They can be compared, which is what the calculation is for.
Risk is central to most real decisions.

questions.stem: What is the quickest way to use opportunity cost to earn an evaluation mark?
options: Add one sentence naming the specific alternative the business gives up by following your recommendation
Define opportunity cost at the start of every answer
List every possible alternative the business has
Avoid making a recommendation at all
questions.why: Naming the specific thing forgone, using the source, is application, analysis and evaluation in a single sentence, and it works on almost any recommendation in the paper.
whyNot: A definition earns knowledge at best, and repeating it wastes time.
Only the next best alternative matters, and listing everything is not evaluation.
Questions that ask for a judgement require one.

questions.stem: A guesthouse owner opens a second property on another island. What is the most significant opportunity cost?
options: Their own presence at the first property, which its reputation was built on
The cost of the second building
The interest on the loan
The wages of the new staff
questions.why: The capital and the wages are financial costs. The opportunity cost is what the owner's divided attention gives up at the original property, which is a genuine growth-against-control trade-off.
whyNot: That is a financial cost, not the benefit forgone.
Also a financial cost.
Also a financial cost.
